A Court Overrules Paris Police and the Crowds Return

Macron Says the Ultra Left Wants to Bring Down the Republic

descs.t: France has banned some protests as riots spread across the country, and Macron says weekend demonstrations will be limited to union marches only. In Paris a court lifted a police ban and thousands gathered anyway. We walk through what the new curbs say and what happened on the streets.

Emmanuel Macron is tightening curbs on protests in France and blaming the hard left for the unrest, as Reuters and the BBC report. A Paris court then lifted a police ban and thousands came out again. We look at who Macron is pointing at, what the bans allow, and whether they can hold.

France is in its worst run of riots in years: shops looted, a McDonald's trashed in Paris, and Macron now says seditious ultra-left groups wanted to bring down the Republic. His answer is a crackdown on protests. We go through what he is banning, who he blames, and what it means for France.

intro.plain: France has started banning protests. After days of riots, Macron says weekend demonstrations will be limited to union marches only. Then a court in Paris lifted a police ban, and thousands gathered anyway. So the government is cracking down and the courts are pushing back. Tell me in the chat: should a government be allowed to ban protests during riots?
intro.mid: Macron is blaming the hard left for the riots in France and he is tightening the rules on protests. Weekend marches are now limited to unions. But a Paris court just overturned a police ban, and the crowds came back. So who is really behind this unrest? Drop your answer in the chat: is Macron right about the ultra left?
intro.bold: France is on fire and Macron has had enough. He says seditious ultra-left groups were behind the riots and wanted to bring down the Republic. Shops looted, a McDonald's smashed in Paris, and now protests are being banned. But a court just let the crowds back out. Tell me in the chat: is this crackdown too little, too late?

hook.plain: France is now banning some protests after nationwide riots, and a Paris court has already overturned one of those bans. Here is what the new rules say and what happened next.
hook.mid: Macron says the hard left is behind France's riots. His answer is a ban on most protests. A court just pushed back. Here is the fight over who controls France's streets.
hook.bold: Shops looted, a McDonald's smashed, and Macron says the ultra left wanted to bring down the Republic. Now he is banning protests. Here is whether the crackdown can actually work.

descs.t: Early in-person voting is underway in South Carolina, Arizona, Georgia and Colorado, and President Trump is urging voters to return mail-in ballots now. Florida's Day 4 count came in at R+16.1 and Harris County, Texas passed about 327,000 early votes through Day 3. We walk through the first early vote numbers state by state.

Trump's early voting push meets the first real numbers: Florida Republicans led Day 4 at 48.5% to 32.4%, while Pennsylvania returned ballots show Republicans behind by 309,952. Here is what the early vote says about the Senate races in Texas, Michigan and Alaska, and what it cannot tell us yet.

Early voting is underway across the country and both sides are fighting over every ballot. Florida shows R+16.1, Pennsylvania shows a 309,952 ballot hole for Republicans, and claims about voting machines switching votes are spreading on X. We sort the numbers from the noise and show voters what to check before they cast a ballot.

intro.plain: Early in-person voting is now underway in South Carolina, Arizona, Georgia and Colorado, and President Trump is telling voters to return mail-in ballots immediately. Florida's Day 4 came in at R+16.1, while Pennsylvania's returned ballots show Republicans behind by 309,952. So the early numbers point in two directions. Tell me in the chat: have you voted yet, and which state are you in?
intro.mid: Trump is pushing early voting state by state, and the first numbers are in. Florida Republicans led Day 4 by more than 16 points. Harris County in Texas passed about 327,000 early votes through Day 3. But Pennsylvania returned ballots show a 309,952 gap for Republicans. Which of these numbers matters most to you? Drop it in the chat.
intro.bold: Early voting is underway and this fight is happening right now. Florida is R+16.1 on Day 4. Pennsylvania has Republicans down 309,952 on returned ballots. And claims about voting machines switching votes are spreading fast. Nothing is decided yet. So tell me in the chat: is Pennsylvania the state that decides this, or is it Texas?

hook.plain: Early in-person voting is underway in South Carolina, Arizona, Georgia and Colorado. Here is what the first numbers from Florida, Texas and Pennsylvania actually show.
hook.mid: Florida Republicans led Day 4 of early voting at R+16.1. Pennsylvania shows them 309,952 ballots behind. Two states, two stories. Here is how to read both.
hook.bold: Trump says go vote now, Florida is R+16.1, and Pennsylvania has Republicans down 309,952. Meanwhile, voting machine claims are flooding X. Here is what is real and what voters should check.

descs.t: Russia launched three waves of ballistic missiles at Kyiv overnight, 21 missiles in all, according to President Zelensky, and Ukraine is now dealing with the aftermath in its cities. We go through what Zelensky reported and what the attack means for Ukraine.

Russia's latest missile attack on Kyiv came as Zelensky accused Trump of blaming him rather than Putin for rising diesel prices, and as Petr Pavel said a truce with Russia had been very close until sanctions on Russian diesel were lifted. We walk through the strikes and the fight over who is responsible.

Zelensky says Russian "humanitarians" fired 21 missiles at Kyiv in three waves overnight, while he insists that Ukraine is not Russia and that refusing to see it is what did Putin in. We look at the strikes, the diesel sanctions argument and who Trump blames.

intro.plain: Overnight, Russia launched three waves of ballistic missiles at Kyiv. President Zelensky says 21 missiles were used, and Ukraine is now dealing with the aftermath in its cities. At the same time, Zelensky says Trump is blaming him, not Putin, for rising diesel prices. Tell me in the chat: who do you think is responsible for the war dragging on?
intro.mid: Russia fired 21 ballistic missiles at Kyiv overnight, in three waves, according to Zelensky. And Petr Pavel says a truce was very close until sanctions on Russian diesel were lifted. Zelensky says Trump is pinning the problem on him instead of Putin. So here is my question for the chat: does pressure on Moscow work, or not?
intro.bold: Russia hit Kyiv with three waves of ballistic missiles overnight. 21 missiles. Zelensky calls them Russian "humanitarians", and he says Ukraine is not Russia, and that refusing to accept that is what did Putin in. Meanwhile the fight over who gets the blame keeps growing. Tell me in the chat: should the sanctions on Russian diesel come back?

hook.plain: Overnight, Russia fired three waves of ballistic missiles at Kyiv, 21 missiles in all. Here is what Zelensky reported and what Ukraine is dealing with now.
hook.mid: 21 missiles on Kyiv overnight, and Petr Pavel saying a truce was very close until sanctions on Russian diesel were lifted. Here is what both mean.
hook.bold: Three waves. 21 ballistic missiles. One city. Zelensky says Ukraine is not Russia, and Putin's missiles have not changed that. Here is the night Russia struck Kyiv.

descs.t: Virginia state Sen. L. Louise Lucas has been charged with drug trafficking and money laundering, the Justice Department says, and seven people were arrested or surrendered in the case. We go through what prosecutors allege and what happens next.

Louise Lucas, the Democratic President Pro Tempore of the Virginia Senate, is in federal custody on RICO, drug trafficking, money laundering, fraud and firearms charges. Her lawyer calls it political payback, and AG Todd Blanche says the Justice Department does not do political paybacks. We walk through the indictment and both sides of that fight.

An FBI wiretap allegedly caught Virginia state Sen. Louise Lucas saying "This is our last chance at generational wealth." Now the lawmaker who pushed to redraw Virginia's congressional maps faces federal RICO and money laundering charges. We go through what prosecutors say the enterprise did.

intro.plain: Virginia state Senator Louise Lucas has been arrested and charged with drug trafficking and money laundering, according to the Justice Department. Seven people were arrested or surrendered in the case, which prosecutors describe as a RICO conspiracy. These are charges, not a conviction. Tell me in the chat: did you expect this, and what should Virginia Democrats do now?
intro.mid: The President Pro Tempore of the Virginia Senate, Louise Lucas, is now in federal custody. Prosecutors say she ran a marijuana trafficking and money laundering enterprise. Her lawyer calls it political payback. AG Todd Blanche says they do not do political paybacks. So who do you believe? Tell me in the chat.
intro.bold: "This is our last chance at generational wealth." That is what Virginia state Senator Louise Lucas allegedly said on an FBI wiretap. Now she is under arrest on RICO, drug trafficking and money laundering charges, the same lawmaker who pushed to redraw Virginia's congressional maps. Tell me in the chat: should she resign right now?

hook.plain: Virginia state Senator Louise Lucas, 82, has been charged with drug trafficking and money laundering. Here is what federal prosecutors say she did.
hook.mid: Prosecutors call it a RICO enterprise. Her lawyer calls it political payback. Here is the federal case against Virginia's Louise Lucas.
hook.bold: "Our last chance at generational wealth." Prosecutors say Louise Lucas said that on an FBI wiretap. Here is how one of Virginia's most powerful Democrats ended up in federal custody.

descs.t: Asked by reporters whether she married her brother, Rep. Ilhan Omar answered "not to my knowledge," and President Trump mocked the answer overnight. We go through what she said, the DOJ court filing in Judicial Watch's request to unseal her search warrant, and where the investigation stands.

Ilhan Omar's "not to my knowledge" answer drew fire from Trump, while legal expert Jonathan Turley says she refuses to admit the investigations into her started under Biden. We walk through the DOJ filing, the raid on her home and what is claim and what is on record.

A simple question, and Ilhan Omar did not say no. Her "not to my knowledge" answer has Trump and her critics pouncing, and a DOJ filing over her sealed search warrant has added fuel. We look at her own words, the filing and what she still has not answered.

intro.plain: Reporters asked Ilhan Omar whether she married her brother, and her answer was "not to my knowledge." Overnight, President Trump mocked that answer. There is also a DOJ court filing after Judicial Watch asked to unseal her search warrant. These are claims and filings, not a verdict. Tell me in the chat: what should she have said?
intro.mid: Ilhan Omar was asked a yes or no question about whether she married her brother. Her answer: "not to my knowledge." Trump jumped on it, and Jonathan Turley says she will not admit the investigations into her began under Biden. So is this a real scandal, or a distraction? Tell me in the chat.
intro.bold: "Not to my knowledge." That is what Ilhan Omar said when asked if she married her brother. Not no. Not never. Trump is mocking it, Judicial Watch wants her search warrant unsealed, and a DOJ filing is out. Tell me in the chat: if the answer is no, why not just say no?

hook.plain: Ilhan Omar was asked if she married her brother. She said "not to my knowledge." Here is what she said, how Trump answered, and what the DOJ filing shows.
hook.mid: Four words, "not to my knowledge," and now Trump, Turley and a DOJ filing are all part of the Ilhan Omar story. Here is what is on record.
hook.bold: A yes or no question, and Ilhan Omar did not say no. Here is her exact answer, the DOJ filing on her sealed warrant, and what she still has not said.

descs.t: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu has ordered the IDF and Mossad to pursue the overthrow of Iran's regime, according to reports carried by the New York Post and other outlets. Separate reports say Israel and the US have drawn up plans to target Iranian nuclear sites. We go through what has been reported and what comes next.

Netanyahu's order to the IDF and Mossad to pursue regime change in Iran comes as Iran threatens US bases over shipping in the region and reportedly activates its Mosaic Defense doctrine. We walk through the order, the strike reports, Kharg Island and how Tehran is reacting.

Israel has put the end of the Islamic Republic on its agenda: Netanyahu has ordered the IDF and Mossad to pursue the regime's overthrow, according to reports. Tehran is threatening US bases and reportedly preparing for a joint strike. We look at what this means for the regime and for the Iranian people who want it gone.

intro.plain: Big news on Iran. Reports say Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu has ordered the IDF and Mossad to pursue the overthrow of the Iranian regime. Other reports say Israel and the US have drawn up plans to target Iran's nuclear sites. And Iran says it will attack US bases over shipping in the region. Tell me in the chat: is regime change finally on the way?
intro.mid: Netanyahu has reportedly ordered the IDF and Mossad to pursue the overthrow of the Islamic Republic. Meanwhile, Iranian officials have reportedly activated their Mosaic Defense doctrine, and Iran is threatening US bases. This is a different level from strikes on sites. So my question for the chat: what should Iranians inside the country do if this happens?
intro.bold: This is the news so many Iranians have waited for. Netanyahu has reportedly ordered the IDF and Mossad to pursue the overthrow of the regime in Tehran. The regime is threatening US bases and reportedly bracing for a joint strike. They are scared, and they should be. Tell me in the chat: are you ready for an Iran without the Islamic Republic?

hook.plain: Reports say Netanyahu has ordered the IDF and Mossad to pursue the overthrow of Iran's regime. Here is what has been reported, and how Tehran is responding.
hook.mid: An order to the IDF and Mossad, strike plans on nuclear sites, and Iran threatening US bases. Here is what Netanyahu's reported order means for the regime.
hook.bold: Netanyahu has reportedly told the IDF and Mossad to go after the regime itself, not just its weapons. Tehran is bracing. Here is why this time could be different.
